facts.text: On this day in 1605, Guy Fawkes was arrested beneath the House of Lords with 36 barrels of gunpowder — enough to level the building and kill everyone inside.
On this day in 1872, Susan B. Anthony voted in a U.S. presidential election and was arrested two weeks later. She was fined $100, which she never paid.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth, packing over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any city in Europe or the Americas.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Bangkok than outside it — over half the world's population falls within that single ring.
Canada has more lakes than every other country combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface lake water within its borders.

On Nov 5, 1991, Robert Maxwell fell from his yacht and drowned — within days, his empire collapsed and $460M in pension funds was found looted. The Mirror Group's 32,000 retirees nearly lost everything.

On Nov 5, 1895, George Selden received the first U.S. patent for a gasoline-powered automobile. He never built one — he just licensed the patent and collected royalties from every carmaker in America for 16 years.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 with 24 brokers and 5 securities. It is now the world's largest exchange by market cap, listing over $25 trillion in equities.

Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway originally made textiles. Buffett bought it out of spite after its CEO tried to lowball him on a share repurchase — a decision he later called the most expensive mistake of his life.

Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6B, making it the largest in history. It was so large that the entire London Stock Exchange's total market cap at the time was smaller than Aramco's opening-day valuation.

On this date in 1955, the first successful kidney transplant between non-twins was performed. The organ survived because the donor and recipient were fraternal twins — close enough genetically to fool the immune system.

On November 5, 1990, astronomers confirmed that the Milky Way's central bar extends further than thought. We live inside a barred spiral galaxy, orbiting a structure so large light takes 27,000 years just to reach us from its core.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces almost all its atoms over seven to ten years, yet the pattern that makes you recognizably you persists. Identity is a process, not a substance.
Octopuses have three hearts, blue blood, and neurons distributed throughout their arms — meaning each limb can taste, touch, and partially think on its own.
On this day in 1605, Guy Fawkes was arrested beneath Parliament with 36 barrels of gunpowder. The plot failed because an anonymous letter warned a lord to stay home.
On this day in 1872, Susan B. Anthony voted in a U.S. presidential election. She was arrested two weeks later and fined $100, which she never paid.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 26 years before the transcontinental railroad was completed. You could theoretically fax someone before you could train across America.
Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire by roughly 300 years. When Montezuma took the throne, Oxford dons had already been arguing about Aristotle for centuries.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was separated from the pyramids by more years than separate her from us.
Meraki (μεράκι): Greek for doing something with soul, creativity, and love — leaving a piece of yourself in your work. No clean English equivalent exists.
Sonder: the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined in 2012 by John Koenig; already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. The longing contains grief, love, and a place that may only exist in the imagination.
On this day in 1605, Guy Fawkes was arrested beneath Parliament. His name, once a synonym for 'fellow' in English slang, became permanently synonymous with the plot he nearly carried out.

On this day in 1872, Susan B. Anthony voted illegally in Rochester, NY. The act was called 'contumacious' by prosecutors — a word meaning stubbornly resistant to authority, from Latin contumacia, pride.
On this date in 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had already burned over 1 million ETH since August — destroying more ETH than miners were creating, making it briefly deflationary.
On Nov 5, 2013, Vitalik Buterin published the original Ethereum whitepaper. He was 19 years old and had already concluded Bitcoin's scripting language was too limited to build on.
Bitcoin's UTXO model means your wallet balance doesn't technically exist — the protocol only tracks unspent outputs, and your 'balance' is software summing outputs assigned to your keys.
The DAO hack in 2016 didn't exploit Solidity — it exploited a reentrancy pattern where the contract sent ETH before updating its internal balance, a logic error, not a language flaw.
Satoshi's genesis block contains the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — both a timestamp and an editorial statement embedded permanently in the chain.
On this date in 1968, 2001: A Space Odyssey had been in theaters for six months — HAL 9000's lip-reading ability quietly predicted a capability real neural networks wouldn't match until 2016.
On this date in 2016, Microsoft announced it had achieved human parity on the Switchboard speech recognition benchmark, hitting 5.9% word error rate — a threshold researchers had chased for 25 years.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed more electricity than 10,000 US households use in a year, yet the resulting weights fit on a hard drive you could hold in one hand.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire known proteome — in roughly 18 months. The previous experimental database took 50 years to accumulate 170,000 entries.

The first neural network trained by backpropagation to outperform humans on a specific task was LeNet-5 in 1998, reading handwritten ZIP codes for the US Postal Service at roughly one million envelopes per day.
